26. The writ-petitioners, however, denied to have received any of the letters. They further said that their office was transferred to the Rangs Bhaban before 1998, To prove service, the said writ-respondents annexed photocopy of the acknowledgments to their supplementary affidavit. It appears therefrom that on 8-4-1999 someone on behalf of the writ-petitioners received the mail addressed to the writ-petitioners which was addressed at 68 Purana Paltan, Dhaka. Another mail addressed to 68 Purana Paltan appears to have been received on 13-9-1998 by one A Rahim on behalf of the writ-petitioners. The sanction letter was issued to the writ-petitioners to the address at 68 Purana Paltan, Dhaka. The writ- respondent wanted to rely on the acknowledgment dated 8-4-1999 to say that the notice for show cause dated 8-4-1999 was sent by the said mail and received by the writ-petitioners. But no record was produced to prove that the writ petitioners left the house at 68 Purana Paltan or that recipients are not their employees or men. So, when the mail was properly addressed, there-is every reason for holding the presumption that it reached the addressee and was a good service as provided in section 27 of the General Clauses Act. 

 64. It appears apparent from the record that the impugned order (Annexure-F) has been preceded by show-cause notices but the writ-petitioners for the reason best known to it alleged that they have not received the show-cause notices. It appears from the notice that the same clearly spelt out the reason for showing cause but the writ-petitioner- respondents without showing cause for the reason best known to them ignored the notices and failed to reply thereto. The said issuance of notices has the presumption of service as it was issued at the notified address of the writ-petitioner as in the case of impugned order which has been admittedly to have been served at the above notified address at 68 Purana Paltan. The impugned letter of cancellation itself refers to the show cause notice which specified the violation committed by the writ-petitioners vide Annexure-12 stating that on 8-4-1999 the RAJUK by referring to its earlier letter clearly indicated the reason for service of notices i.e. the carrying out of construction of building in excess of the 6th storied building and similarly, by Annexure-10 dated 13-8-1998 informed the Writ-petitioners that the construction of any building in excess of the permissible limit would be a positive hindrance to air-navigation and requested the writ-petitioners to stop the construction and obtain necessary approval from the concerned authorities. It is also apparent from Annexure-11 that the writ petitioners are also aware of the restriction as apparent from the letter issued by the RAJUK. It is to be noted that admittedly the writ-petitioners have failed to obtain any permission from the Civil Aviation Authority as required under the law for any construction of building over maximum permissible height in view of the location of the building from the runway /funnel.
